item.title: 17-19 Clarence Road, Kilburn, NW67TG, 21st August
item.description:
I am writing to formally report a mature Council-managed street tree immediately outside our property at 17-19 Clarence Road, Kilburn, and to request an urgent joint inspection by the Council’s Tree Team. There is now substantial visible damage in the immediate vicinity of the tree which raises concerns both about continuing damage to our property and the safety and condition of the public footway. I have attached photographs showing the current condition. 1. Significant cracking to the boundary wall The brick boundary wall immediately adjacent to the street tree has developed a substantial stepped crack through multiple courses of brickwork and mortar. The cracking is concentrated in the section of wall close to the mature tree and appears consistent with significant movement of the wall. Given the size and proximity of the tree and its root zone, I am concerned that root growth and/or associated ground movement may be contributing to the damage. I appreciate that the precise cause must be professionally established, and I therefore request that the Council inspect the tree, its root zone and the damaged wall and determine whether the Council-owned tree is causing or materially contributing to the movement. 2. Significant displacement and deterioration of the public footway The public footway surrounding the tree is also visibly uneven and extensively patched. There are changes in level and deterioration around the tree/root area which appear to indicate continuing movement beneath the pavement. This creates a potential trip and accessibility hazard for pedestrians and raises a separate highways safety concern irrespective of the damage to the boundary wall. Please therefore arrange for the Highways team to inspect the footway and formally assess its condition and safety. 3. Continuing risk of damage The tree is mature and is positioned extremely close to both the public footway and our boundary wall. The concern is not simply the existing cosmetic appearance of the wall. If root growth or tree-related ground movement is responsible for the damage, repairing the wall or resurfacing the pavement without addressing the underlying cause is unlikely to provide a durable solution. I therefore request that the Council considers removal and appropriate replacement of this tree as part of its assessment, rather than simply undertaking another localised pavement repair or pruning the canopy where that would not address the cause of the damage. The property is within a conservation area. We are conscious of the importance of retaining mature trees where reasonably possible. However, conservation considerations should be balanced against the visible property damage, highway displacement, pedestrian safety and risk of further deterioration in this particular location.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Clarence Road, London
Report on FixMyStreet
